learningObjective: Map each root-to-leaf rule path to one axis-aligned region of feature space and its constant leaf prediction.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can align exact threshold lines in two-dimensional feature space with the corresponding rule nodes and leaves. Showing both representations at once makes recursive partitioning and piecewise-constant prediction directly traceable without interaction.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: Mermaid could render the rule tree, but cannot precisely align full-region and child-region threshold lines with the feature-space rectangles they create.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: fixed geometry pairs one partition with its exact tree, distinguishes a full-height root cut from a child-only cut, and supports a visible prediction path.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: nested lists or a table could express the rules and leaf probabilities, but would not reveal their equivalence to axis-aligned spatial regions.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: letting readers move a point or threshold could teach sensitivity, but introduces controls and hidden states when one labelled point and simultaneous plot/tree views already expose the core mapping.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: CART and textbook treatments contain tree and partition figures, while scikit-learn publishes rendered examples, but no external composition is needed and no permissive figure-adaptation grant was established for the book artwork. No source figure, coordinates, data, or layout is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose explains recursive threshold tests and constant leaves separately, leaving readers to mentally construct how a path intersects half-spaces into one region and why a child split affects only its parent's region.

pages.insight: The preceding K-nearest-neighbor slide contrasts instance-based classification with learned rules, but contains no recursive partition or decision-tree mechanism.

The Random Forests slide defines a decision tree as if-then statements that split feature space one attribute at a time, describes entropy reduction, includes Gini code, and then shifts to bootstrap aggregation. It does not spatially connect a rule path to nested feature-space regions.
The dedicated split-criterion slide lists variance, information gain, and Gini impurity by target type, but provides no worked candidate split, recursive geometry, or leaf prediction.

The following gradient-boosting slide describes trees as weak models dividing inputs into regions by rules or thresholds, then moves to sequential residual correction rather than explaining a single tree's partition.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed page by page for decision tree, random forest, gradient boosting, XGBoost, CART, Gini, entropy, information gain, and feature-space splitting. Pages 24-27 are the only contiguous decision-tree teaching neighborhood: pages 25-26 directly discuss tree training, while pages 24 and 27 establish the neighboring methods. Page 131 mentions gradient boosting only as a hybrid-recommender combiner and adds no tree mechanism. No deck artwork, code, wording, coordinates, or layout is reused.

sources.title: Classification and Regression Trees
sources.usage: Used as the authoritative CART source for recursive binary partitioning, axis-aligned feature-threshold tests, constant terminal-node predictions, greedy split construction, and pruning context.
sources.license: The book is commercially published and no permissive license for reproducing or adapting its figures was identified. No figure, example data, wording, coordinates, or layout is reused.

sources.title: scikit-learn User Guide: Decision Trees
sources.usage: Used as official implementation documentation to verify left and right partitions for a feature-threshold pair, weighted child impurity, greedy exhaustive best-split search, recursive application, and class probability as the class fraction at a terminal node.
sources.license: scikit-learn documentation is distributed with the BSD 3-Clause licensed project. It is cited for semantics only; no documentation figure, Iris data, code, prose, or visual layout is reproduced.

sources.title: The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd Edition
sources.usage: Used as an authoritative textbook cross-check for recursive binary partitioning into rectangular regions, constant models within terminal regions, greedy top-down construction, and the high variance of individual trees.
sources.license: A free author-hosted PDF is available for reading, but free access is not treated as permission to adapt textbook artwork. No textbook figure, dataset, wording, coordinates, or layout is copied.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is the equivalence of the tree and the partition: the root threshold cuts the entire active region, each descendant threshold cuts only the samples and subregion reaching that node, and the conjunction of path tests defines one axis-aligned terminal rectangle. The original synthetic example has eight training points, with four circles and four triangles. The left leaf contains three circles and one triangle, so P(triangle) = 1/4. The right child separates three lower triangles from one upper circle, producing probabilities 1 and 0. The highlighted point follows x1 > 4 and x2 <= 3 to the pure-triangle leaf. Shapes, labels, and line extent—not color—encode every logical distinction.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the exact decision-tree neighborhood, then checked CART, official scikit-learn mathematics, and an authoritative statistical-learning textbook before selecting an original paired partition-and-rule-tree SVG.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description. Class 0 uses circles, class 1 uses triangles, the root cut is solid and full-height, the child cut is dashed and confined to its parent region, and rule outcomes and probabilities are directly labelled. The 360-unit viewBox scales with the established plot-panel primitive and has no minimum width for readability at 390 CSS pixels; existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast and shared print rules force a light high-contrast palette.
